summary:
HEARTBEAT OF EARTH is an interactive web platform that brings together Earth science, music, and storytelling to help people connect with our planet.
We wanted to find a creative way to make scientific information more interesting and easier to understand. Our project uses NASA Earth observations and environmental data, including temperature changes, atmospheric CO₂ levels, and historical sea-ice changes, to help users explore what is happening to our planet.
Through an interactive experience, users can discover important Earth events, explore scientific information, and connect environmental changes with music through data-inspired soundscapes.
We believe that science doesn't always have to be explained through numbers and graphs. By combining technology, music, and real-world data, we hope to make people more curious about Earth, help them understand environmental changes, and remind everyone why protecting our planet matters.
details:
HEARTBEAT OF EARTH – The Earth Information Jukebox is a project we created with the idea of bringing science and music together. We wanted to find a different way for people to understand our planet and learn about the changes happening around it. Our website allows users to explore Earth through information about temperature changes, atmospheric CO₂ levels, sea-ice variations, and NASA's Earth observation missions. We have brought these different elements together in an interactive platform where users can explore environmental events and experience the connection between scientific data and music. The idea behind our project is simple: scientific information should not feel difficult or boring to explore. Instead of showing people only numbers and graphs, we wanted to make the experience more interesting through visuals, music, and storytelling. We hope this will encourage more people, especially students, to become curious about Earth and understand the importance of protecting it.

We developed the project using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Node.js, and web-based development tools. We also used GitHub for managing our code and Vercel to host our website. Our project is completely software-based and does not require any additional hardware. What makes this project special to us is the combination of two things that people connect with in different ways: science and music. While developing it, we considered how easy the website would be to use, how the information could be presented clearly, and how it would work on different devices.

Through HEARTBEAT OF EARTH, we hope to make people look at our planet a little differently. We don't just want users to see environmental changes through data; we want them to connect with the story behind that data and understand why our Earth deserves attention and care.
